title: Fold compress(decompress(x)) pairs in compressed materialization
reasons: abandoned by the implementer after investigation
summary: I added the fold to CompressedMaterialization::CreateCompressProjection in src/optimizer/compressed_materialization.cpp. When the child is a LogicalProjection whose expression is __internal_decompress_integral_* (compressed type T_c, offset m), and the new compress expression is __internal_compress_integral_* producing T_c with the same non-NULL offset m, the change swaps the decompress argument into the child projection and has the compress projection pass a plain colref of type T_c. It keeps the compress stats, and it skips the fold if any other compress expression references the binding. It builds, and both projections are gone from the q13 EXPLAIN. The time does not go away, though. Bench on q13 was 467.9 → 465.8 ms (-0.4%, inside noise). In the profile the decompress projection's ~0.16s CPU disappears, but PERFECT_HASH_GROUP_BY rises from 0.43s to 0.58–0.60s. The work moves rather than disappearing, so I'm abandoning.
notes: The decompress projection was not pure overhead. It also gave the aggregate flat vectors. Without it, the perfect hash aggregate gets the RIGHT hash join's output directly, which is probably sliced or dictionary vectors. Its sink costs about as much more as the projection used to cost (+0.17s vs -0.16s). Follow-up idea: first give the perfect HA sink a cheap path for dictionary or selection-vector group and aggregate input, then retry this fold. The fold code is small and correct as written (offset and type checks, NULL offsets excluded). Saved as memory cm-fold-decompress-compress-no-gain.
